title: Petra and the Garden
premise: Edmund Whitlock, youngest ledger-keeper of the Guild of Small Impossibilities, discovers the guild's founding secret: their power was borrowed from a bound entity wearing the king's body, and every gift the guild trades is a payment on that ancient debt. When the crown's witch-hunters burn the guildhall, Edmund flees with the ledgers and the guild's last living founder, Petra, a gardener whose memory holds the binding words. To end the hunt, they must reach the capital before midwinter and unbind the king—even though doing so will strip every guild member of their gift, including Edmund's own. In the frozen throne room, Edmund chooses memory over power: the king is freed, the guild dissolves into ordinary life, and Petra plants the first spring garden in a world that must now grow things the slow way.
about_author: Dominic Nakamura is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging the correspondence of obscure nineteenth-century trading societies, an experience that seeps into every ledger and secret in his fiction. He writes from a drafty house in the Pacific Northwest, where he keeps a garden that refuses, stubbornly, to be impossible.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the guildhall's cellar, Edmund balances the books of impossible trades—a jar of last year's sunlight, a borrowed grief—and notices entries in his own handwriting he never made. His mentor dismisses it as fatigue. The beat is quiet unease: the comfort of routine beginning to curdle into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Crown Proclaims
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The royal herald declares a hunt for the gifted, and the guild's elders vote to scatter and hide. Petra, the ancient gardener who tends the guildhall's impossible orchard, alone argues they must act. Edmund watches her stand against fear. The beat is the first fracture: invisibility failing as a strategy.

chapters.title: Entries in a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Investigating the phantom ledger entries, Edmund finds they record trades made by the guild's founder—dead two hundred years—and each entry is dated in the future. The final one reads: 'The guildhall burns. The ledger survives.' The beat is dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Orchard Keeps Its Promises
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Witch-hunters reach the city walls. Petra shows Edmund the orchard's heart: a tree that grows pages, and on them, the truth of the guild's founding—a bargain struck with the thing beneath the crown. The beat is revelation and inheritance: Edmund learns what he has truly inherited.

chapters.title: Ash on the Snow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The guildhall burns as the founder's entry foretold; the elders die or scatter, and Edmund escapes through the cellar with the ledgers while Petra holds the hunters with the last of her garden's magic. The beat is grief and survival—the cost of staying visible at last.

chapters.title: The Road of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Fleeing north through a winter country where neighbors inform on neighbors, Edmund and Petra shelter with a woman who once sold her sorrow to the guild and wants it back. Edmund returns it, illegally, and feels the gift's pull. The beat is temptation: power offered as comfort.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the capital's shadow, Petra confesses she was there at the founding—that the bound king was once her friend, and she helped bind him to save the world from his gift. The beat is guilt unburdened: the corrupting logic of necessary power, passed down like an heirloom.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The hunt's chief inquisitor—himself secretly gifted, sustained by the crown-thing—captures them and offers Edmund his mentor's stolen life in exchange for the ledgers. Edmund refuses, and they are dragged toward the throne room as the solstice storm breaks. The beat is despair at the lowest point, with refusal as a small stubborn flame.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the frozen throne room, Petra begins the unbinding while Edmund reads the counter-ledger, trading every scrap of the guild's stored power to hold the crown-thing at bay. The king wakes inside his own body and speaks his own name. The beat is the climax: sacrifice, memory, and the choice of ordinary over mighty.

chapters.title: The First Spring Garden
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with a closing passage in Edmund's. The guild is dissolved; the gifted live unremarkable lives, and Edmund keeps an ordinary bookshop with the old ledgers as history. Petra, finally mortal, plants a garden that will grow the slow way. The beat is resolution and quiet hope: inheritance remade as memory instead of power.
